a2-b115: A token dose may not be enough to make the jaw release. More than once, I've dissolved Dead Sea magnesium chloride hexahydrate flakes in water and taken about one gram per minute by mouth for around twenty minutes before mine fully released. I use magnesium chloride because it's absorbed far better than magnesium oxide, and I can usually see it start helping within a minute. Around twenty grams is fine for my gut, and I've only had diarrhea above about forty grams. Magnesium chloride is also less likely to cause diarrhea than several other kinds of magnesium, including the ones people take on purpose as laxatives.
a2-b117: Magnesium taken before the MDMA peak also makes the peak less euphoric for me, which makes me think the magnesium calms some of the MDMA's stimulation, besides meeting a need for magnesium that's rising fast. I'm fine trading a little euphoria for a relaxed jaw, since in my experience the jaw relaxing comes with a much lower risk of the MDMA toxicity symptoms.
a2-b120: If someone has impaired kidneys, they do need to be more cautious with large, rapid magnesium doses like my one-gram-per-minute approach, because they may not clear magnesium normally. But the MDMA is a far bigger danger to their kidneys, since besides overheating them and causing dangerous electrolyte shifts, it can injure the kidneys directly (acute kidney injury) and through rhabdomyolysis, which is muscle breaking down into the blood. So kidney trouble is a strong reason not to take MDMA, and if they've taken it anyway, their worsening jaw tension still needs treating. With serious kidney impairment, though, I'd treat it as a higher-risk case and get help sooner, and I wouldn't have them copy my approach blindly.
his-b118ds: My second wife had severe convulsions after an MDMA overdose. At the hospital,  they figured out what caused that: her potassium was found to be critically low, and IV potassium was the only treatment they gave her. That experience is what leads me to treat serious MDMA toxicity as a broader electrolyte emergency, although magnesium is still the first and most useful supplement to give once the jaw tenses, since potassium gets depleted after magnesium.
